items.en: Tajikistan moves to leave ICC amid US push against court
items.zh: 塔吉克啟動退出國際刑事法院程序
items.summary: Tajikistan has moved to withdraw from the International Criminal Court. The step follows an ICC finding that Tajikistan failed to comply with the court's request to arrest Russian President Vladimir Putin, and it comes while the United States is pressing states to distance themselves from the court. A withdrawal would thin the ICC's membership in Central Asia and weaken enforcement of the warrant against Putin in the region. Al Jazeera frames the move as part of a wider pattern of pressure on the court's authority rather than an isolated national decision.

items.en: COP31: What next after UN climate talks collapse
items.zh: COP31 氣候談判破局，下一步未明
items.summary: UN member states failed to agree on how to fast-track action to reverse global warming, and the COP31 summit in Turkiye closed without a final deal. Al Jazeera reports it was the longest UN climate summit on record and the first in 17 years to end without an agreed outcome. Negotiators could not bridge differences over the pace of moving away from fossil fuels and over who pays for the transition. The collapse leaves the next steps for the global climate agenda unclear and shifts attention to action taken outside the formal UN process.

items.en: Israeli strikes kill at least three, including UNRWA worker, in Gaza
items.zh: 以軍空襲加薩，至少三死含一名 UNRWA 員工
items.summary: Israeli strikes across Gaza killed at least three people, among them a staff member of UNRWA, the UN agency for Palestinian refugees. Al Jazeera reports that Israel has continued to launch attacks across the territory despite the ceasefire deal reached in October 2025. The death of a UN worker adds to concerns about the safety of humanitarian staff in Gaza, where aid agencies say movement and access remain difficult. The incident underlines how fragile the ceasefire has become, with repeated strikes reported since it took effect.

items.en: Iran says it will use 'all available means' to counter US blockade
items.zh: 伊朗稱將用一切手段反制美國封鎖
items.summary: Iran's foreign ministry said the country will use all available means to confront what it calls a United States naval siege and to defend itself. Al Jazeera reports the statement sets out Tehran's position that it will contest the blockade rather than accept it. The wording raises the risk of confrontation at sea in and around the Gulf, a corridor that carries a large share of the world's seaborne energy trade. The exchange adds to an already tense standoff between Tehran and Washington.

items.en: Search continues for dozens missing after Indonesia candy factory fire
items.zh: 印尼糖果廠大火，數十人仍失蹤待搜救
items.summary: Rescuers in Banten, Indonesia are still searching for around 30 workers missing after a fire swept through a candy factory. At least 24 people have been confirmed dead. Al Jazeera reports the search has continued since the blaze broke out, with families waiting for news of those unaccounted for. Industrial fires with high casualty counts have repeatedly raised questions about workplace safety enforcement and building standards in Indonesian manufacturing, where large workforces are concentrated in single-structure plants.

items.en: AI boom drives hiring demand beyond tech sector: Report
items.zh: AI 熱潮把徵才需求擴散到非科技產業
items.summary: A joint report from Taiwan's Institute for Information Industry and job bank 1111 says AI development is pulling hiring demand into industries outside tech. Job openings in chemical manufacturing, which supplies materials such as glass cloth and copper-clad laminate for AI hardware, rose 74.32 percent from the first to the third quarter of 2026, the largest gain among major industries. Warehousing and transport support services rose 44.83 percent and architectural design 24.57 percent. Within tech, AI engineer openings rose 66.12 percent and algorithm development 54.41 percent.

items.en: Taiwan banks deploy AI to prevent cyberattacks
items.zh: 台灣銀行業用 AI 防堵網路攻擊
items.summary: Taiwan's domestic banks are increasingly using AI to spot suspicious activity, find system weaknesses and defend against cyberattacks as attacks on the financial sector grow. Taiwan Cooperative Bank reported roughly double its 2025 monthly average of suspicious external probes in the first ten months of 2026, with about 80 percent of attacks falling between August and October. First Bank's web application firewall blocked about 2.2 million attacks from January to October. One consultant suggested using AI to simulate attacks and find weaknesses before hackers do.

items.en: Can we build a more ethical AI future?
items.zh: 我們能打造更有倫理的 AI 未來嗎？
items.summary: In this UpFront episode, Marc Lamont Hill talks with tech entrepreneur Anil Dash, a former adviser to the White House Office of Digital Strategy, about AI's risks and about who is accountable for them. The discussion covers the economic and privacy effects of the current AI boom and whether the money flowing into the sector is sustainable. Al Jazeera's framing points to recent turmoil in the industry, including leadership upheaval at Nvidia, a wave of technology outages affecting government, banking and aviation, and Anthropic's market debut at a two trillion dollar valuation.

items.en: Liverpool thrash 10-man Man United in nightmare start for Pochettino
items.zh: 利物浦 4-0 痛宰十人曼聯，波切提諾惡夢開局
items.summary: Liverpool beat Manchester United 4-0 in the Premier League, with United reduced to ten men during the match. Al Jazeera reports the result made for a nightmare start to Mauricio Pochettino's time in charge at Old Trafford, with the scoreline leaving little doubt about the gap between the sides on the day. The heavy defeat puts immediate pressure on the new manager and on a squad that has struggled for consistency, while Liverpool take the points and the momentum from a fixture that shapes the mood of both clubs' seasons.

items.en: 'That was crazy': Verstappen wins Las Vegas GP for third time in four years
items.zh: 維斯塔潘四年三度奪下拉斯維加斯大獎賽
items.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen held off Kimi Antonelli and George Russell to win the Las Vegas Grand Prix, his third victory at the race in four years. Al Jazeera reports the race featured 35 lead changes, an unusually high number that made the result hard to call until late. Verstappen described the race as crazy. The win reinforces his command of a circuit that rewards straight-line speed and tyre management, and keeps Red Bull in the conversation at a point in the calendar where small margins decide standings.

items.en: Wembanyama's 50 points, 19 rebounds lead Spurs to 14th win of NBA season
items.zh: 溫班亞瑪 50 分 19 籃板，馬刺收下本季第 14 勝
items.summary: Victor Wembanyama scored 50 points and pulled down 19 rebounds as the San Antonio Spurs recorded their 14th win of the NBA season. Al Jazeera notes the tally sits just short of his career high of 52 points, set against Dallas on 4 November. The performance continues a run of dominant scoring and rebounding nights that have made the French centre the central figure of San Antonio's season, and adds to the case that he is operating at a level few players in the league can match this year.

items.en: Inside the talks between student protest leaders and Macron's government
items.zh: 法國學運領袖與馬克宏政府談判實錄
items.summary: Al Jazeera interviews French high-school student leaders who have met President Emmanuel Macron, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu and Education Minister Edouard Geffray. The movement has run for about two months, with school blockades and street protests. Marius Mensil, 17, says officials listen and smile but make no concrete commitments, calling the concessions offered a few crumbs. Students want Parcoursup rebuilt, failing school buildings repaired, more permanent teachers and an extra ten billion euros for education. The government has recruited 920 substitute teachers, plans 3,000 more, and will cap class sizes at 28 in the most disadvantaged schools from 2027.

items.en: Sudan's war leaves disabled children missing out on education
items.zh: 蘇丹戰火讓身心障礙兒童失學
items.summary: Al Jazeera reports from Khartoum that Sudan's war has left many children with disabilities without schooling or therapy. Four-year-old Muzan Abdelrahman, who has a hearing impairment, cannot get specialised support because the rehabilitation centres her family relied on have closed. UNICEF says at least eight million school-age children lack formal education, and about 30 percent of schools were not operating as of August. Sudan had more than 230 schools for disabled children before the war, many now shut. Advocates call for a national survey of dropouts, reopened special centres, Braille and sign-language resources, and inclusive teacher training.

items.en: Taiwanese stop-motion animation episode wins top prize in Japan
items.zh: 台灣定格動畫奪日本賞大獎，教孩子理解差異
items.summary: An episode of the Taiwanese stop-motion series Pai Pai won the Grand Prix at the 53rd Japan Prize, NHK's international competition for educational content, at a ceremony in Tokyo. The winning 12-minute episode, Typhoon's Coming, follows a ten-year-old who hopes school will be cancelled because of a typhoon, only to discover that her friends feel differently about it. Made by TurnRhino Original Design Studio with Public Television Service, the series uses children's everyday interactions to show that people react differently to the same situation, encouraging empathy. The competition drew 415 entries from 59 countries and regions.

items.en: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
items.zh: 輝達董事會讓黃仁勳回任執行長
items.summary: Nvidia's board has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Al Jazeera reports he had stepped down earlier this month after revelations of at least two affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The reversal ends a short period of interim leadership at the company at the centre of the AI hardware supply chain. Markets read the return as a stabilising signal: Taiwanese suppliers tied to Nvidia's roadmap rallied sharply on the news, and chip indices posted outsized gains in the session that followed the announcement.

items.en: Artificial superintelligence 'arriving', warns top Meta executive
items.zh: Meta 高層警告：超級智慧正在到來
items.summary: Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang warned that artificial superintelligence is arriving. He posted on Sunday after an Anthropic employee said he had used Claude to solve the Riemann hypothesis, arguing the result shows emerging models will be clearly superhuman at improving themselves and at accelerating research in biology, armaments and economics. Wang said how humanity acts over the next year will matter greatly, criticised lazy thinking that treats superintelligence as inevitable, and said controlling AI with unconstrained recursive self-improvement is unlikely. The article contrasts his position with Mark Zuckerberg's more optimistic stance.

items.en: Nvidia supply-chain expansion boosts confidence among Taiwan firms: Analyst
items.zh: 輝達擴大供應鏈承諾，台廠信心回升
items.summary: Nvidia said it is expanding long-term commitments to supply-chain partners including TSMC, Hon Hai, SPIL, Kinsus, King Yuan and Unimicron, as well as Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Amkor and Ibiden. The expansion covers added substrate capacity, more output from existing plants and more packaging capacity, using TSMC's 5nm and 3nm nodes and CoWoS packaging. An analyst at the Taiwan Institute of Economic Research said this gives Taiwanese suppliers better order visibility for Vera Rubin chips, and noted Nvidia's overall supply commitments have reached 390 billion US dollars.

items.en: Fujii Kaze piano recital Day 2 show also to be livestreamed on YouTube
items.zh: 藤井風鋼琴獨奏會 Day2 加碼 YouTube 直播
items.summary: Billboard JAPAN reports that the Day 2 performance of Fujii Kaze's solo piano-and-vocal recital was added as an emergency YouTube livestream, following the same treatment given to the first night. The recital is a stripped-back format built around piano and voice rather than a full band, a setting the artist has used before for intimate shows. Opening the second night to a free stream widens access well beyond the venue, which matters for overseas fans in Taiwan and Hong Kong who cannot attend Japanese dates in person.

items.en: RADWIMPS release first live video of 'Yuzutsu' from fan club tour extra show
items.zh: RADWIMPS 公開〈夕星〉FC 巡演加場首度現場影像
items.summary: Billboard JAPAN reports that RADWIMPS have released the first live performance video of the song Yuzutsu, filmed at an additional date on their fan club tour. The track was released digitally on 2 October 2026 as a film tie-in, and this is its first live airing to be made public. Fan club tour footage is usually kept inside the membership, so putting the video out publicly extends the song's reach ahead of wider touring and gives non-members a first look at how it is staged.

items.en: YOASOBI's new song 'KILLA', arranged by Tsumiki, debuts on Top Japan Hits by Women
items.zh: YOASOBI 新曲〈KILLA〉登上 Top Japan Hits by Women
items.summary: Billboard JAPAN reports that YOASOBI's new song KILLA has entered the Billboard JAPAN x Spotify playlist Top Japan Hits by Women as a new addition in the 20 November update. The track is arranged by Tsumiki rather than by Ayase alone, a collaboration that marks a shift in the duo's production credits. Placement on a Spotify-partnered chart playlist is a meaningful early signal for streaming momentum, which is the main driver of chart position for YOASOBI releases.
